## Introduction

192: BER vs MMR based on Sygnal signatures

## 1. read derived table, check names and sructure anmd draw barplots


```{r}

# Load the data
data <- read.csv('SingleMoleculeData.txt', sep = '\t')

filtered_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(BreakPoint3) & !is.na(BreakPoint5) & BreakPoint3 != '/' & BreakPoint5 != '/') %>%
  filter(as.numeric(BreakPoint3) > 0 & as.numeric(BreakPoint5) > 0)

# Check table of SampleID
table(filtered_data$SampleID)

# Convert BreakPoint3 and BreakPoint5 to numeric (if needed)
filtered_data$BreakPoint3 <- as.numeric(filtered_data$BreakPoint3)
filtered_data$BreakPoint5 <- as.numeric(filtered_data$BreakPoint5)

### PLOT

# Create a new column to classify samples as either 'Disrupted' or 'Perfect'
filtered_data$Category <- ifelse(filtered_data$SampleID %in% c('86fDisrupted', '91mDisrupted'), 'Disrupted', 'Perfect')

# Set circle parameters
center_x <- 13453
center_y <- 8476
radius <- 225

# Count the number of grey (Perfect) and red (Disrupted) dots within the circle
within_circle <- filtered_data %>%
  filter((BreakPoint3 - center_x)^2 + (BreakPoint5 - center_y)^2 <= radius^2)

# Count the dots
count_grey <- sum(within_circle$Category == 'Perfect')  # Count grey dots
count_red <- sum(within_circle$Category == 'Disrupted')  # Count red dots

# Print the counts
cat("Number of grey dots within the circle:", count_grey, "\n")
cat("Number of red dots within the circle:", count_red, "\n")

# Create data for the circle
circle_data <- data.frame(
  x = center_x + radius * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 450)),
  y = center_y + radius * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 450))
)

# Create scatterplot with semi-transparent colors and the square
ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = BreakPoint3, y = BreakPoint5, color = Category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +  # Make points semi-transparent (alpha = 0.5)
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(NA, 12000)) +  # Limit Y-axis to max of 12000
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(11000, NA)) +  # Limit X-axis to min of 11000
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Disrupted" = "red", "Perfect" = "grey")) +  # Use red and grey for the two categories
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of BreakPoint3 vs BreakPoint5 by Sample Category", 
       x = "BreakPoint3", 
       y = "BreakPoint5") +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 13447, xmax = 13459, ymin = 8470, ymax = 8482), 
            color = "blue", fill = NA, linetype = "dashed") +  # Add little square with coordinates
  
  # Add circle with dotted line
  geom_path(data = circle_data, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "black", linetype = "dotted") +  # Add green dotted circle
  
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +  # Fix the aspect ratio to make the circle look circular
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")


```

## 2. Additional Plot with Centered Limits

```{r}
# New limits calculation
total_length <- 500

# Calculate the new x and y limits
x_min_new <- center_x - total_length / 2
x_max_new <- center_x + total_length / 2
y_min_new <- center_y - total_length / 2
y_max_new <- center_y + total_length / 2

# Create the scatterplot with updated limits without the square
ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = BreakPoint3, y = BreakPoint5, color = Category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 1, size = 2, position = position_jitter(width = 40, height = 40)) +  # Increase transparency and size, add jitter
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min_new, y_max_new)) +  # New Y-axis limits
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(x_min_new, x_max_new)) +  # New X-axis limits
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Disrupted" = "red", "Perfect" = "grey")) +  # Use bright red and grey for the two categories
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of BreakPoint3 vs BreakPoint5 by Sample Category (Centered)", 
       x = "BreakPoint3", 
       y = "BreakPoint5") +
  
  # Add circle with dotted line
  geom_path(data = circle_data, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "black", linetype = "dotted") +  # Add green dotted circle
  
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +  # Fix the aspect ratio to make the circle look circular
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor grid lines for a cleaner look
        panel.grid.major = element_blank())  # Remove major grid lines for a cleaner look
```

## 3. Random Permutation Test

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Define the number of permutations
num_permutations <- 10000

# Initialize counters
count_same_or_less <- 0

# Total counts for comparison
total_red <- count_red  # 2 red dots
total_grey <- count_grey  # 18 grey dots

# Combine categories into a vector for permutation
categories <- rep(c("Disrupted", "Perfect"), times = c(total_red, total_grey))

# Perform permutations
for (i in 1:num_permutations) {
  # Shuffle the category labels
  shuffled_categories <- sample(categories)
  
  # Count the number of red (Disrupted) dots within the circle
  red_within_circle <- sum(shuffled_categories[1:total_red] == "Disrupted")
  
  # Check if the count of red dots is less than or equal to the observed count
  if (red_within_circle <= total_red) {
    count_same_or_less <- count_same_or_less + 1
  }
}

# Calculate the proportion of permutations that had the same or fewer red dots
proportion_same_or_less <- count_same_or_less / num_permutations

# Print the results
cat("Proportion of random permutations with", total_red, "or fewer red dots:", proportion_same_or_less, "\n")
```
